parsed.restated: ∃ (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (Tstar : ℝ) (v : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ), InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀ ∧ HasCompactSupport u₀ ∧ u₀ ≠ 0 ∧ Tstar ∈ Set.Ioc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On (Ico 0 Tstar) u₀ v p ∧ (∃ E : ℝ, ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) Tstar, (∫ x : ℝ³, ‖v x t‖ ^ 2) < E) ∧ (∀ T : ℝ, 0 < T → ((∃ w q, EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On (Icc 0 T) u₀ w q) ↔ T < Tstar)) ∧ (∀ T ∈ Ioo 0 Tstar, (⨆ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) T, velocityC1Norm (v · t)) < ⊤ ∧ (∫⁻ t in Ico (0 : ℝ) T, vorticityNorm (v · t)) < ⊤) ∧ Filter.limsup (fun t : ℝ => velocityC1Norm (v · t)) (𝓝[<] Tstar) = ⊤ ∧ (∫⁻ t in Ico (0 : ℝ) Tstar, vorticityNorm (v · t)) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ (w : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (q : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ), ¬ EulerExistenceAndSmoothnessR3 u₀ w q
parsed.english: There exist nonzero, compactly supported, smooth, rapidly decaying, divergence-free initial data u₀, a maximal time Tstar in (0,1], and a smooth finite-energy Euler solution (v,p) on [0,Tstar). Closed-interval Sobolev solutions exist exactly for T < Tstar. C¹ norms and the vorticity integral are finite on every [0,T] with T < Tstar. The C¹ norm has limsup ⊤ at Tstar, and the vorticity integral over [0,Tstar) is infinite. For every pair (w,q), it is not a global smooth finite-energy Euler solution with data u₀.
parsed.why_clearer: It states the range of Tstar as the interval (0,1] and writes the final nonexistence as an explicit 'for all (w,q), not a solution' instead of a negated existential.
